items.note: The identity $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=u*v/S^2$ is derived along the paper's route: the substitution in the Fourier sum, tensoring, commuting with pointwise products, then the convolution rule and $F^+F=I/S$.

'Substituting $w'=\beta w$ ... gives $\frac1q\sum_{w'}z_{w'}e^{2\pi i w'\beta^{-1}j/q}$, which is $(R_\beta^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$': this is the paper's substitution $h=ck$, written out correctly for a unit $\beta$.

'Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, and $R$ applies $R_{t_i}$ on axis $i$, so tensoring gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$'. The page skips the intermediate $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$, but it is immediate.

The page derives $F_q^+F_q=I/q$ from orthogonality of characters and tensors it to $I/S$. Like the paper, it recalls the normalized convolution rule $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ without proof.
'so this equals $\frac1SF_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=u*v/S^2$' combines the two normalizations exactly as the paper does.

errors.problem: The restatement of Lemma no-sort-resampling drops that the approximations $\widetilde A,\widetilde B_0$ have error less than $p^2$. The page later claims 'error below $dp^2$', and this per-axis bound is its only source, so it is never stated on the page.

errors.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$ (so $\gcd(s_i,t_i)=1$ for odd $s_i$).
errors.problem: $\gcd(s_i,t_i)=1$ is a hypothesis of the resampling lemma and is what makes $t_i$ a unit modulo $s_i$ in the cancellation. The page leaves the case $s_i=2$ open instead of requiring odd primes. The paper chooses distinct odd primes $s_i$, so every $\gcd(s_i,t_i)=1$.
